mainTopic: The order of the relatives in the משנה's list, and the precise wording of פוטרות and מן החליצה ומן הייבום
overview: The גמרא continues explaining why the משנה opens its list with בתו. All fifteen relatives need a דרשה for their יבום exemption, but only for בתו (a daughter from rape) is even the basic איסור learned through a דרשה, from the גזירה שוה links הנה–הנה and זמה–זמה. When this approach runs into trouble over where אחות אשה and the sister cases are placed, the גמרא drops it. In its place, it explains that the תנא lists the women by closeness of relation. He keeps related groups together, such as three generations, or sisters and siblings, even when that bends the order slightly. Next the גמרא examines the משנה's wording. It says פוטרות rather than אוסרות, because the צרה needs no חליצה and is forbidden only where the מצוה of יבום applies. It mentions both חליצה and יבום to teach that whoever is not fit for יבום does not need חליצה either. It lists חליצה first because the משנה follows אבא שאול, who gives חליצה priority. Finally, the גמרא asks what the exact numbers in the משנה come to exclude, and the answers come on the next amud.

steps.title: But every case in the list comes from a derivation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that בתו comes first because it is learned through a דרשה. Every relative in the משנה is exempt from יבום only because of a דרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But all of them also come from a derivation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation it just gave for why the משנה starts with בתו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said a דרשה-based law is 'dear' to the תנא, so he lists it first. But the rule that any ערוה is exempt from יבום (and so is her צרה) is itself learned through a דרשה from אחות אשה. So that reason should apply to every case, not just to בתו.

keyTerms.meaning: from a derivation (a דרשה of the פסוקים)

phrases.english: All of them also come from a derivation!
phrases.notes: He means all fifteen relatives in the משנה. Their exemption from יבום is learned through a דרשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanation (from before this section) that בתו comes first because דרשה-based laws are dear.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בתו is listed first because it is learned through a דרשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'derived through a דרשה' is the reason for coming first, it does not single out בתו, since every case's יבום exemption is learned through a דרשה.

steps.title: Only for the daughter is the basic prohibition itself derived
steps.stepSummary: The other relatives' basic איסור is written openly in the תורה, and only their יבום exemption is learned through a דרשה. For בתו, the basic איסור itself comes from a דרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that, for the matter of יבום, they come from a derivation. But their main prohibition is written openly about them. For his daughter, the main prohibition itself comes from a derivation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating two levels: the basic איסור, and the יבום exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case needs a דרשה for the יבום exemption, but that is shared by all. What makes בתו special is that even the basic איסור of being with her is never written openly. So בתו is 'more' דרשה-based than the others and earns first place.

phrases.english: Granted that, regarding the matter of levirate marriage,
they come from a derivation,
their main prohibition is written explicitly about them.
His daughter: the main prohibition comes from a derivation.
phrases.notes: This is his daughter from a woman he raped. The תורה never openly forbids her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two levels of derivation (the basic איסור versus the יבום exemption)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All the cases are equally דרשה-based, so בתו has no special reason to come first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only בתו needs a דרשה even for its basic איסור, so it is the most דרשה-dependent case and comes first.
steps.whatToRemember: Two levels: (1) Is the basic איסור written openly? (2) Is the יבום exemption written openly? For בתו, both come from a דרשה.

steps.title: The source for the daughter's prohibition: two גזירה שוה links
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב יצחק בר אבדימי: the איסור of בתו is learned from a גזירה שוה on the word הנה, and her punishment of burning is learned from a גזירה שוה on the word זמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: רב יצחק בר אבדימי told me: it is learned from 'הנה' and 'הנה', and it is learned from 'זמה' and 'זמה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim that the איסור of בתו comes only from a דרשה, by showing where that דרשה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הנה appears about a daughter's daughter (ויקרא 18:10) and about a woman and her daughter (ויקרא 18:17). Linking them teaches that one's own daughter, even from rape, is forbidden. The word זמה (ויקרא 18:17 and 20:14) links to the punishment, so this איסור carries burning.

keyTerms.meaning: it comes, it is learned (used for a גזירה שוה)
'they are', a word used to link two פסוקים
'wickedness', a word used to link two פסוקים
a law learned by linking a shared word in two פסוקים

phrases.english: As Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לִי רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said to me:
It is derived from 'hena' and 'hena',
it is derived from 'wickedness' and 'wickedness'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17 and ויקרא 20:14. This second link teaches the punishment of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא אֲמַר לִי רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 by showing the דרשה that the איסור of בתו depends on.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the basic איסור of בתו comes only from a דרשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא, quoting רב יצחק בר אבדימי: the גזירה שוה of הנה–הנה and זמה–זמה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a daughter from one's wife. That case is covered by the איסור of a woman and her daughter. This is a daughter born from a rape, whom no פסוק mentions openly.

steps.title: Then the wife's sister should come last
steps.stepSummary: If דרשה-based cases are dear and come first, then אחות אשה, the openly written source case, should be placed at the very end of the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said that anything that comes from a derivation is dear to him, let him teach the wife's sister last!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the 'dear derivation' principle one step further and asks about the order of the rest of the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבום exemption for all the relatives is learned from אחות אשה, where the תורה says it openly. So אחות אשה is the least דרשה-dependent case. By the תנא's own logic it should come last, yet the משנה lists it in the middle.

phrases.english: Now that you have said
that any matter that comes from a derivation
is dear to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the תנא of the משנה.

phrases.english: let him teach the wife's sister last!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ כׇּל מִלְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא מִדְּרָשָׁא חַבִּיבָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the accepted principle from steps 1–3 to question the placement of another case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The placement of אחות אשתו in the middle of the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If דרשה-based cases come first, the openly written source case should logically be placed last.

steps.title: The wife's sister is grouped with the other sisters
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה was already listing 'sister' prohibitions, it put אחות אשתו together with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he was dealing with the prohibition of sisters, he taught his wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the order here follows topic grouping, not the 'dear derivation' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists אחותו מאמו and אחות אמו, and right after them comes אחות אשתו. Keeping all the 'sister' cases together outweighs moving אחות אשה to the end. So the 'dear derivation' rule explains what comes first, but grouping by topic can still decide where other cases go.

keyTerms.meaning: since, because (he was already on that topic)

phrases.english: Since he was dealing with the prohibition of sisters,
he taught his wife's sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחות אשה should be last because it is the openly written source.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is placed among the other sister cases because the תנא was already on that topic.
steps.whatToRemember: For now, the order is explained this way: בתו comes first because even its basic איסור comes only from a דרשה, and אחות אשה sits in the middle because it belongs with the other sisters. Step 6 challenges this, and step 7 replaces it with a different reason for the order.

steps.title: Then put the whole sister section at the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 5. If the sisters were grouped only to keep them with אחות אשתו, the whole sister group should have gone to the end of the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let the תנא teach this whole section at the end!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If the sisters were grouped together just so אחות אשתו could join them, then the whole group should have been moved to the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said אחות אשתו was moved up to sit next to the other sisters. But the grouping could have worked the other way: move all the sisters down to the end next to אחות אשתו. Then אחות אשתו stays last, as the 'dear cases first' rule needs. Since the משנה did not do this, the 'dear cases first' idea looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: A section or group of cases

phrases.english: But let him teach this section at the end!
phrases.notes: 'This section' means the group of sister cases, which could all have gone last together with the wife's sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 5 answer that אחות אשתו was moved up to join the other sister cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grouping could just as easily have moved all the sisters down to the end. That would keep the openly written case last, so the 'dear cases first' order is not being followed.

steps.title: New rule: the list follows closeness of relation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the דרשה-based approach. The תנא lists the women by how closely related they are: first his own descendants, then his wife's descendants, then her ancestors.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא arranged the list by closeness. He taught his daughter, his daughter's daughter, and his son's daughter, who are his own relatives. Since he taught three generations below him, he also taught three generations below her (his wife). And since he taught three generations below her, he taught three generations above her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the old idea and offers a brand-new reason for the order. The list goes from the closest relatives to less close ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His own daughter and granddaughters are his blood relatives, so they come first. Next come his wife's daughter and granddaughters, keeping the 'three generations down' pattern. Then come her mother and grandmothers, three generations up, so the wife's family is finished together.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer for a new one)
By closeness, from the closest relative onward
Since, because he was already dealing with

steps.whyThisMatters: This new 'closeness' rule replaces the דרשה approach. It is used for the rest of the explanation of the משנה's order.

phrases.english: Rather:
the tanna arranged them by closeness:

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא בִּתּוֹ וּבַת בִּתּוֹ וּבַת בְּנוֹ,
phrases.english: he taught his daughter, his daughter's daughter, and his son's daughter,
who are his own relatives.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת לְמַטָּה דִּידֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And since he taught three generations below him,

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא נָמֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת לְמַטָּה דִּידַהּ.
phrases.english: he also taught three generations below her.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת לְמַטָּה דִּידַהּ,
phrases.english: And since he taught three generations below her,
he taught three generations above her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by replacing the whole 'דרשה cases first' approach
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier explanation with a new ordering principle (closeness of relation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order follows which cases come from a דרשה and are 'dear'
steps.terutzMaskana: The order follows closeness of relation, with related groups of generations kept together

steps.title: Sisters next, and the wife's sister joins them
steps.stepSummary: After the generations, the תנא lists his sister and his mother's sister, who are his blood relatives. He then adds אחות אשתו because he is already dealing with sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he taught his sister and his mother's sister, who are his own relatives. And since he was dealing with the prohibition of sisters, he taught his wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues walking through the list using the closeness rule. It explains where the sisters fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His sister and aunt are blood relatives, but less close than his daughters, so they come later. אחות אשתו is not his blood relative. She is placed here only because the topic is already 'sisters'. This also answers step 6: the sisters sit where closeness puts them, not at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition involving sisters or siblings
He was dealing with, talking about

phrases.english: And he taught his sister and his mother's sister
who are his own relatives.
And since he was dealing with the prohibition of sisters,
he taught his wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנָא אֲחוֹתוֹ וַאֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ דִּקְרוֹבֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues applying the closeness rule of step 7 to the next cases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Continues the new ordering principle and adds a topic-grouping exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחות אשתו is out of place, since she is not a blood relative
steps.terutzMaskana: She is placed with the sisters because the topic is already sisters

steps.title: By right, the daughter-in-law should come earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a problem with the closeness rule. כלתו should come before אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, since that brother's wife is not forbidden because of closeness at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by right he should have placed his daughter-in-law before the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime, since it is not because of closeness that she is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one case in the list seems to break the closeness rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the closeness rule, a related woman like כלתו should come before a woman whose איסור has nothing to do with closeness. אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו is forbidden for a different reason, not because she is close family. Yet the משנה lists her first.

keyTerms.meaning: And by right, it would make sense that
The wife of his brother who was not alive at the same time as him

phrases.english: And by right he should have placed his daughter-in-law first

phrases.aramaic: מִקַּמֵּי אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
phrases.english: before the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime,
since it is not because of closeness that she is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds a case where the closeness rule seems not to be followed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כלתו is forbidden because of a family tie, so she should come before a woman forbidden for a reason unrelated to closeness.

steps.title: The brother's wife was kept with the sibling cases
steps.stepSummary: The תנא was already dealing with sibling cases, so he listed the brother's wife there. Only after that did he list כלתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, since he was dealing with the prohibition of siblings, he taught the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime, and then he taught his daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 9 with the same 'keep the topic together' idea it used for אחות אשתו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother's wife still involves a sibling (his brother). So she was placed right after the other sibling cases, and כלתו was pushed to the very end. The closeness rule holds, with the small exception of topic grouping.
steps.whatToRemember: The order of the משנה follows closeness of relation. When the תנא is in the middle of a topic, like sisters or siblings, he finishes that topic first, even for cases that are less close.

phrases.english: However, since he was dealing with the prohibition of siblings,

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
phrases.english: he taught the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime,
and then he taught his daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Topic grouping overrides strict closeness order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלתו should be listed before the brother's wife
steps.terutzMaskana: The brother's wife goes with the sibling cases, and כלתו comes after them

steps.title: Why say 'exempt' and not 'forbid'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the wording of the משנה. Why does it say these women פוטרות their צרות, instead of the stronger word אוסרות?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did he specifically teach 'exempt'? Let him teach 'forbid'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: the exact word the משנה chose. It asks why the weaker-sounding word 'exempt' was used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צרות are not just free from יבום; they are actually forbidden to the brother. So 'forbid' seems to describe their status more fully, and the גמרא asks why the משנה did not use it.

phrases.english: And why did he specifically teach 'exempt'?
Let him teach 'forbid'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the order of the list and opens a new question about wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice of the word פוטרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The צרות are actually forbidden to the brother, so אוסרות seems the more accurate word.

steps.title: 'Forbid' could suggest she still needs חליצה
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה said אוסרות, one might think יבום is forbidden but חליצה is still needed. Saying פוטרות teaches that she is free from everything, even חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had taught 'forbid,' I would have said that she is forbidden to do יבום, but as for חליצה, she must do חליצה. So the word 'exempt' teaches us that she is fully free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'exempt' is actually the stronger word here. It tells us that she needs no חליצה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Forbid' only rules out יבום. It leaves open the idea that a חליצה is still needed. 'Exempt' means she has no tie to the brother at all, so neither יבום nor חליצה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
It teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: פוטרות means the צרה is completely free. She needs no יבום and no חליצה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'exempt' is weaker than 'forbid' here. In this case 'exempt' teaches more: she is free even from חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: a צרה of one of these women may remarry without חליצה.

phrases.english: If he had taught 'forbid,'
I would have said it is forbidden to do yibum,
but as for chalitza, she must do chalitza.
So it teaches us.
phrases.notes: By saying 'exempt,' the משנה teaches that she does not need חליצה either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the chosen word teaches more than the suggested one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With אוסרות, one would think only יבום is forbidden and חליצה is still required
steps.terutzMaskana: פוטרות teaches full exemption from both יבום and חליצה

steps.title: Why not say she is forbidden to do חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: If the צרה is free even from חליצה, the משנה should have said plainly that she is forbidden to do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה say: 'She is forbidden to do חליצה!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 12. If the point is that she needs no חליצה at all, why not use a clear word of prohibition?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said פוטרות was chosen so we know she is free even from חליצה. The challenge here is that a phrase like 'forbidden to do חליצה' would have said that even more clearly. So why the softer word פוטרות?

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him (the תנא) teach / say
She is forbidden to do חליצה
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום

phrases.english: Then let him teach: 'She is forbidden to do חליצה!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 12 by suggesting stronger wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the word פוטרות in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the goal is to show she needs no חליצה, a clear prohibition would show that better than 'exempt'.

steps.title: חליצה is not really a forbidden act
steps.stepSummary: You cannot call חליצה 'forbidden', because by itself it is just taking off a shoe. What wrong has he done?
steps.simpleTranslation: What has he done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'forbidden' would not fit. A useless חליצה is not a sin; nothing bad happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה on its own is only the woman removing the man's shoe. If it is done when not needed, it simply has no effect, so the משנה could not call it 'forbidden'.

phrases.english: What has he done?
phrases.notes: He means: if they do חליצה anyway, it is only taking off a shoe, so nothing wrong happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by saying 'forbidden' is the wrong word for חליצה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the suggested wording as legally inaccurate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could have said 'forbidden to do חליצה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unneeded חליצה is not a forbidden act, so that wording does not fit.

steps.title: A needless חליצה does lead to a real problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the last answer: there is a danger. If people see her doing חליצה, they may think she could also do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? If you say she does חליצה, people will think she can also do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 14. Doing חליצה here is not harmless, because it can mislead people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Onlookers who see the צרה doing חליצה will assume she is part of the יבום system. Then they may think another brother could marry her in יבום, which is truly forbidden. So there is a reason to call חליצה forbidden after all, and step 14's answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: She can be married in יבום

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying she really may do יבום. It is saying people might wrongly think so if they saw her do חליצה.

phrases.english: Why not?
If you say 'she does חליצה',
then she can be married in יבום!
phrases.notes: This is what people would wrongly conclude from seeing her do חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that a needless חליצה is harmless.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that people may conclude the צרה is also fit for יבום.

steps.title: The צרה is only forbidden where there is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says פוטרות because the צרה is not forbidden on her own; she is forbidden only in the setting of the מצוה of יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the צרה is forbidden only where there is a מצוה of יבום, and where there is no מצוה she is permitted, that is why the משנה says 'exempt'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to step 13. The word 'forbidden' would make the צרה sound forbidden in general, which is not true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she were the widow of a man not related to him, he could marry her normally. The ban on the צרה comes only from the יבום situation. So the משנה says she is 'exempt' from יבום, not that she is 'forbidden' as a person.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where the מצוה of יבום applies
Co-wife (another wife of the same dead husband)

steps.whatToRemember: פוטרות was chosen because the צרה's ban exists only inside the מצוה of יבום, not as a general prohibition.

phrases.english: Since it is in a case of מצוה
that the co-wife is forbidden,
and where there is no מצוה she is permitted,
for that reason he teaches 'they exempt'.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּבִמְקוֹם מִצְוָה הוּא דַּאֲסִירָה צָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 rejected step 14's answer, this gives a new reason why the משנה says פוטרות rather than any 'prohibit' wording. It answers both step 11 and step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording by the nature of the prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have used a prohibition word.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Exempt' is more accurate, because the צרה is forbidden only in the מצוה setting.

steps.title: Why mention both חליצה and יבום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists both חליצה and יבום, when 'exempt from יבום' alone should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does the משנה say 'from חליצה and from יבום'? Let it say 'from יבום' alone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to another wording question in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that if she is free from יבום, it is obvious she needs no חליצה either. So the word חליצה looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Marrying the widow of a brother who died childless

phrases.english: And why specifically does he teach
'from חליצה and from יבום'?
Let him teach 'from יבום' alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new wording question about the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase מן החליצה ומן הייבום in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'from יבום' should be enough, so mentioning חליצה seems extra.

steps.title: No יבום means no חליצה
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה said only 'from יבום', we might think she still needs חליצה. Listing both teaches that חליצה applies only where יבום could apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it said only 'from יבום', I would think she does חליצה but cannot do יבום. The משנה teaches us that whoever is fit for יבום is fit for חליצה, and whoever is not fit for יבום is not fit for חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 17. The word חליצה is needed to block a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without it, one could think the צרה is in a middle state: no יבום, but חליצה still required. The rule given here ties the two together. If יבום is impossible, חליצה has no place either.
steps.whatToRemember: Rule: whoever is fit for יבום is fit for חליצה, and whoever is not fit for יבום does not need חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule links חליצה directly to יבום and is a basic principle in the laws of יבמות.

phrases.english: If he had taught 'from יבום',
I would have thought: to do חליצה, she does חליצה,
but to be married in יבום, she is not.
It teaches us
whoever is fit for יבום is fit for חליצה,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה לַיִּיבּוּם — אֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה לַחֲלִיצָה.
phrases.english: and whoever is not fit for יבום is not fit for חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הוה אמינא / קא משמע לן: the extra word prevents a mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She is free from יבום but still needs חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חליצה applies only where יבום could apply, so she is free from both.

steps.title: Why is חליצה listed first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה does not put יבום first, or else just say 'from חליצה' alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it say 'from יבום and from חליצה', or else just 'from חליצה' alone!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both words are needed, the גמרא asks about their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה mentions יבום first, so we would expect the same order. Also, after the rule in step 18, saying 'from חליצה' alone would already show she is free from יבום too.

phrases.english: Then let him teach 'from יבום and from חליצה',
or else 'from חליצה' alone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 18 and asks about the order of the two words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order 'from חליצה and from יבום' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יבום is the main מצוה and should come first; or 'from חליצה' alone would already cover both.

steps.title: The משנה follows אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows אבא שאול, who holds that the מצוה of חליצה comes before the מצוה of יבום, so חליצה is listed first.
steps.simpleTranslation: This משנה follows אבא שאול, who said: the מצוה of חליצה comes before the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 19 by naming whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבא שאול, חליצה is the preferred choice, so it is natural to list it first.
steps.whatToRemember: The order of the words in the משנה follows אבא שאול: חליצה takes priority over יבום.

phrases.english: It is the view of אבא שאול,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: מִצְוֹת חֲלִיצָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוֹת יַיבּוּם.
phrases.english: who said: the mitzva of חליצה comes before the mitzva of יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the order question of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the משנה to a specific תנא's opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יבום should be listed first, or חליצה alone should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows אבא שאול, who gives חליצה priority, so it is listed first.

steps.title: What do the numbers in the משנה come to leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case is being excluded by the exact count in the רישא, and what is being excluded by the count in the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The count in the first part of the משנה, what does it come to leave out? And the count in the later part, what does it come to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the משנה's wording: why give an exact number? It is setting up the answers that will come next, explaining which cases each number leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה gives an exact count like 'fifteen women,' it signals that only these are included and no others. The גמרא assumes the count must be there to rule out some case we might have thought belongs on the list, and asks what that case is. It asks this twice: once for the count in the רישא and once for the count in the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: A count or number; here, the exact number of cases the משנה lists
The first part of the משנה
The later or last part of the משנה
To leave out what? It asks what case a word or number comes to exclude

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack saying the number is wrong. The גמרא accepts the count and only asks which case it is meant to leave out.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic rule of how the גמרא reads a משנה: an exact number is never just decoration. It always tells us that some case we might have added is not included.

phrases.english: The count of the first part, to exclude what?
phrases.notes: The first part is the opening of the משנה, which says 'fifteen women.'

phrases.english: And the count of the later part, to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving why חליצה is listed before יבום (Step 20), the גמרא moves to a new wording question about the numbers in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is left out by the exact count in the רישא, and which case is left out by the exact count in the סיפא.
